title: Expression
body:
Trying to comprehend the sequences of neuron spikes being set off every millisecond within a fantastical mass of flesh, hammered into shape by millions of years of evolution, years or decades of being exposed to a violently shifting world, and context within the range of basically any amount of time, and then going to simply represent it all comprehensively in a set of 26 characters and some symbols is certainly one of the most absurd things our species has had the nerve to think it can pull off. 

Even the best of writing seems to be no more than a conduit for the writer's style and elegance, and it is far less common across the immense amount of writing that exists that one appreciates the idea more than the way the idea was forced down the throat of language and spit out as characters on your page. Take this very paragraph as an example.

Language seems as though it cannot possibly be representative as the thoughts or reasoning of your mind, and yet we have no better way to communicate. And the worst of it all is that we pick up language, spoken, written, or otherwise, from other people, and then attempt the insane task of translating it as thought. The idea of teaching somebody how to write is almost entirely ridiculous.

Sometimes I think we'd be better off as ants. Those guys know how to get along a lot better than we do.
